Most surprisingly interesting book you've ever read?

Personally, I'd say Plato's Euthyphro. It picks apart the concept of piety--it's actually extraordinarily hard to define. I was surprised because its argumentation was beautiful and worth the tough slog. It also introduced me to Plato as a whole.

I remember when I was first referred to Plato back when I started to become interested in philosophy. I thought it sounded like a boring name and couldn't understand all the hype around it. How wrong was I. Same thing happened with Borges' The Aleph.
Oh, huh! Mind giving me the elevator pitch for The Aleph, then?

Well, the charm about the book is that some of its stories are short enough to count themselves as a (longish) elevator pitch. And any is good enough to prevent you from putting down the book until you've read the rest. http://ddm.ace.ed.ac.uk/project-files/Asterion/story.html

Rousseau's "Confessions" comes to mind -- the guy really tried to bare his soul. Best part: he describes that, as a child, he was under the care of some beautiful nanny who spanked him a lot, and that (reading between the lines), this colored his entire adult sexuality.
I expected Less Than Zero to be nothing more than canned angst and juvenile shock scenes. It was, but it also had some thoughtful perspectives on modern culture, too. A solid 3/5 book.

Mordecai Roshwald's Level 7. It's not a very well known book. but it's one of the most emotionally jarring ones I ever read.

And it can be finished in a few hours, it's just slightly larger than a novella. Definitely recommended if you can get your hands on it.
Catch-22. Dragged at some points but definitely picks up.

*Life a User's Manual *by Georges Perec. My girlfriend read it for an architecture class, and I started reading it to help her with some homework one night. Perec wrote each chapter with a series of constraints generated using a Greco-Roman square, and one of the coolest narratives that emerges involves this ongoing competition between a puzzle-maker and a puzzle-solver. It looks boring, and there are definitely some boring stretches, but man is there some brilliant shit in there. I like to save short quotes from things I like, but I ended up copying out multiple full pages more than once because every sentence was too clever to leave out.

Maybe this isn't what you were looking for but if we're going with honestly surprising I'll say Clive Cussler's Atlantis Found.

Now that you've finished rolling your eyes I'll provide some background. I used to be an insufferable snob when it came to books... well obviously I mean literature because who reads books?

A couple of years ago I was traveling in a non-English speaking country having finished the books I brought with me. (I now see the point of the Kindle) Desperately bored, I hike up to the English "bookstore" and its pretty much Cussler, Sparks, or Patterson. So I pick up Atlantis Found.

Yes it had all the subtlety of a piano being dropped down a flight of stairs but it was a fun read. I've never read any of his other stuff but I have definitely opened myself up to reading more "pulp". I consider myself a better reader for it.

Freakonomics, by Steven Levitt and Stephen Dubner. It was bought for me as a gift. I don't know what I was expecting, except that I didn't really think it was my kind of thing. Absolutely fascinating, would highly recommend to anyone. It is easily digestible, rarely goes above high-school level economics and shows hoe unbelievable interconnected so many things are in this world.

The book that was most surprisingly interesting to read was when my senior literature class read Go Down Moses. It was very difficult at first to get into, but it picked up quickly after my classmates and I spent some more time with it, we also had an amazing teacher.
I was surprised at how much I enjoyed Born to Run. I thought, a book about running how interesting could it be? But I really enjoyed it.

The Thickety by J.A. White. This is a book aimed at grades 5-8. I wanted to read something new to my class last school year. I found the book trailer and it was creepy and dark. I thought this is something that my kids would love. They did. I had several kids go out and buy their own copy. The school librarian bought a few copies and they were always checked out. But, you don't have to take my word for it. ;-)

It takes a certain amount of contributions for a member to downvote an idea. While I agree with the general concept of this, I worry that it favors seniority. As the site becomes bigger, those who have been here longer have an increasing authority on what stays vs. what is buried. You can say that site etiquette would rule against that, but if no one can enforce it, how does that hold up? I think someone with basically site-tenure may find it easier to abuse a system where they're given power over recent users.

I can see how it looks that way, but I believe the feature is more to stop people downvoating just because they disagree with something. It also stops people creating alt accounts with the malicious intention of mass downvoating someone. This feature was also added to encourage lurkers to post comments and get involved with the community, particularly as Voat's userbase wasn't the largest at the time of it's addition.

I imagine that in the near future, if the userbase keeps growing then the threshhold will be reduced.

If illegal content is posted on the sub, it may be taken down. But that's generally the only reason a sub would get taken down. Atko and the administration team strongly believe in being open and transparent about all the actions they do - so we're always kept in the loop unlike at that other place.

I don't know enough about this to say, but I would imagine there are limitations in place to prevent it.

Where is the line between free speech and harassment in terms of the site's policies?

Voat does not want to meddle with the content on the site unless it's illegal in Switzerland. I imagine over time and as more situations arise, we will learn about Voat's stance on harassment as of upto now - no harassment has taken place to my knowledge.

If a site is vitriolic but within site rules, is it allowed to stay?

Yes, as long as there is no illegal content.

What if it fails to break site rules, but is a constant point of site discussion (e.g. an anti-Islam subverse always making the front page)?

The policy is not to meddle, I expect Voat to do that. But again, we will have to wait and see if such a situation were to occur.
